idiom_name: closed variant set + one total match per operation
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: declare one base declaration that names the complete alternative set (sealed/permits, enum, closed class, union, sealed trait, private constructor), give each alternative its own immutable data type, and make every operation a single match over the base declaration with one arm per alternative - the completeness check is the compiler's exhaustiveness analysis, never a default arm. This replaces the accept()/visit() double dispatch of Visitor: the variants carry no operation methods, a new operation is a new match in the code that needs it, and a new variant is a compile-time list of every site that must decide about it. Keep the classic Visitor (or plain per-variant methods) when the element types are contributed from outside the module, when variants change far more often than operations, or when third parties must add operations without touching the hierarchy - closure is a contract, not a free improvement.
code_sketch:
Set = A(payload) | B(payload) | C          # closed variant set, one immutable case each

f(value, ...) = match value:               # one operation = one total match
    A(p) -> ...                            # compiler rejects the build when an arm is missing
    B(p) -> ...
    C    -> ...
pitfalls: A catch-all arm (default/else/_ or a generic lambda) compiles and silently disables the coverage proof for every variant added later.
Closure has to be declared in the language's own construct; a hierarchy that is only closed by convention, comments or review gives no guarantee at all.
Stale artifacts still fail late: an exhaustive match compiled against an older version of the set can throw at run time when the hierarchy gained a case and the match site was not rebuilt.

Wrong move: silencing the non-exhaustive-match warning (@unchecked or Predef.runtimeChecked in Scala, -Wno-switch, a per-file lint disable) to keep the build green -> the site now lies about its coverage and every later variant lands on a match that already skipped one -> instead add the missing arm, and where the set is genuinely open model the openness as an explicit variant, not a muted diagnostic.

Wrong move: declaring a non-sealed / non_exhaustive / non-frozen middle layer in a hierarchy the team fully owns 'just in case' a variant is needed -> coverage of the supertype is lost at every match site and each consumer must handle a case that never occurs -> instead seal what you own and route real third-party extension through a separate, unsealed interface.

Wrong move: putting shared behaviour in a base-class method whose switch keeps a default arm so subclasses can vary it -> that base switch is the very unchecked catch-all the pattern removed, now hidden behind a method call -> instead keep operations as total matches over the closed type and share code through plain helper functions.
